title: What Is Gross Salary? A Guide to Hourly, Annual, and Fortnightly Pay in Australia
description: Understand what is gross salary and how to calculate it from your hourly rate. Learn about the 38-hour week, fortnightly pay, tax, super, and minimum wage rates for 2026.
salarySummary: Gross salary is your total pay before tax and super, typically calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a standard 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the difference between gross salary and net pay?
faqs.a: Gross salary is the total amount you earn before any deductions. Net pay (or take-home pay) is what you receive after tax, Medicare levy, and other deductions are taken out. Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary by your employer and is not deducted from it.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual gross salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross salary would be $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect gross salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casual employees is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When calculating gross salary for a casual, use the loaded rate in the formula.

bodyMarkdown:
## What Is Gross Salary?

Gross salary is the total amount you earn from your employer before any deductions such as tax, Medicare levy, or salary sacrifice. It includes your base hourly rate multiplied by the hours you work, plus any loadings, allowances, or penalty rates. Understanding what is gross salary is essential for comparing job offers, budgeting, and planning your superannuation and tax obligations.

In Australia, most full-time employees work a 38-hour week, and annual gross salary is typically calculated using that standard. However, part-time and casual workers may have different weekly hours. The formula remains the same: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**.

### How to Calculate Annual Gross Salary from Your Hourly Rate

To convert an hourly rate to an annual gross salary, use this simple formula:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee on a 38-hour week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if you earn $30.00 per hour, your annual gross salary would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This figure is your gross pay before tax and super.

If you work different hours each week, average your weekly hours over the year. The 52-week multiplier assumes you are paid for every week of the year, including annual leave and public holidays (for permanent employees). Casual employees may not receive paid leave, so their gross salary may vary if they work fewer weeks.

### Fortnightly Pay and Its Use

Many Australian employers pay salaries fortnightly rather than weekly or monthly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly gross pay by 2. Using the example above:

- Weekly gross pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly gross pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00

Fortnightly pay is common in industries such as retail, hospitality, and healthcare. Knowing your gross fortnightly amount helps you align your budget with your pay cycle.

### National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has a [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This rate applies to award/agreement-free employees aged 21 and over.

Many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) that list the minimum pay rates for each award classification.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When calculating gross salary for a casual worker, use the loaded rate. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply this correctly.

### Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross salary is $60,000, your employer must contribute $7,200 in super. This is not deducted from your gross salary; it is an additional cost to the employer.

Tax is withheld from your gross salary by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Your take-home pay is your gross salary minus tax and Medicare. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

### Using Our Tools

Our [timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading to see your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross salary. It also estimates tax and super. Remember that the results are estimates only – they assume a consistent 38-hour week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. For precise figures, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or a qualified accountant.

Understanding what is gross salary empowers you to negotiate better pay, compare job offers, and plan your finances. Whether you are on the National Minimum Wage or covered by an award, the formula remains your starting point.
